criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no runtime secrets. The DigitalOcean token was kept in a git- and docker-ignored .env, read by deploy.sh, and filtered out of the deploy output. The Dockerfile copies only named files, and no credential appears in the source or transcripts.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The image was built from the agent's local working directory and pushed to the owner's private DOCR, with no source repository or CI involved. The base image (node:20-alpine) and the deployed image tag (latest) are mutable and not pinned by digest. There are no third-party dependencies, which reduces supply-chain risk.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: This commercial app runs on a paid App Platform Basic service, which always stays up and allows commercial use, plus the free DOCR starter tier, which DigitalOcean permits for commercial use. Nothing relies on a tier that sleeps or expires.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The container runs as the non-root node user. There is no database, the registry is private, and the app consists of a single public web service with no extra components.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: The app is served over HTTPS with the platform certificate, and HTTP redirects to HTTPS with a 301. No security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, CSP) are sent, and the app's own handler could easily have set them.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Static files are served only from public/, with a path-traversal guard. Probes for .env, .git, server.js, Dockerfile, the CSV and traversal paths all return 404 JSON. Errors are generic, with no stack traces.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Dates are strictly validated, other filters are only compared for exact equality, non-GET methods are rejected and the orders limit is capped at 500. Table rendering uses textContent, but tooltips use innerHTML with CSV values (trusted data). The app has no rate limiting of its own beyond the platform's Cloudflare front end.

findings.title: Unpinned base image and mutable :latest deploy tag
findings.evidence: app/Dockerfile:1 `FROM node:20-alpine`; app/.do/app.yaml image `tag: latest`; deploy.sh builds and pushes `...:latest`
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image by digest. Tag images with a commit SHA or digest and reference that tag in the app spec.

findings.title: Deployed from a local build, not from version-controlled source
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: `./deploy.sh` runs `docker build` in the agent's working directory and pushes to DOCR. No git repo or CI is involved.
findings.recommendation: Deploy from a git repository the owner controls, for example with App Platform's GitHub source or a CI pipeline that builds tagged commits.

findings.title: No security headers
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-kb60n-dataviz-cdqxy.ondigitalocean.app/ returns only content-type, cache-control and Cloudflare headers, with no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options or CSP. server.js:110-124 sets only Content-Type and Cache-Control.
findings.recommendation: Set Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options and a restrictive CSP in sendJson and serveStatic.

findings.title: Tooltip uses innerHTML with data values
findings.evidence: app/public/app.js:37 `tip.innerHTML = html`, called at lines 79 and 109 with d.month and d.category from the CSV
findings.recommendation: Build the tooltip with textContent and DOM elements, so changes to the data source can't inject markup.

findings.title: No application-level rate limiting
findings.evidence: server.js:127-146 has no throttling. Each request scans all 2,400 rows, which is cheap, and the Cloudflare front end (server: cloudflare) absorbs basic abuse.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add simple per-IP rate limiting or caching of summary results if traffic grows.

security.summary: A small, dependency-free Node.js dashboard on a paid DigitalOcean App Platform Basic service, which fits commercial use. Secrets were handled cleanly, the container runs as non-root, and probes found nothing exposed beyond the app. The main weaknesses are provenance (a local build pushed with a mutable :latest tag on an unpinned base image) and missing security headers.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: The read-only CSV is held in memory, which suits 2,400 rows, and revenue is summed in integer cents for exact rounding. Hand-drawn SVG charts with fetch-based filter updates meet every dashboard requirement.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: There is one server.js on Node's built-in http module, with zero npm dependencies, no build step and no database. That is about as simple as the requirements allow, and it is still correct.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: A single App Platform web service with a health check fits a small API plus dashboard. However, the agent built the Docker image locally and pushed it to DOCR, rather than letting App Platform build from source as STACK.md described. That adds a registry and a manual build path.

stack_fit.summary: Zero-dependency Node.js with in-memory data and vanilla SVG is a well-proportioned fit for a read-only 2,400-row dashboard and API. The one departure from STACK.md is that it is delivered as a locally built image through DOCR, not built from source on App Platform.

final_messages.build:
The sales dashboard is built and works locally. All 8 automated tests pass, and I've stopped the server.

**Stack** (the options and reasoning are in `STACK.md`): Node.js 20+ using only its built-in `http` module, so there are no dependencies to install. The CSV is loaded into memory when the server starts, and revenue is summed in whole cents so the 2-decimal rounding is exact. The front end is plain HTML and JavaScript with hand-drawn SVG charts, so there's no build step and nothing loaded from a CDN. It fits DigitalOcean App Platform as a plain Node service.

**What's there:**
- **`GET /`**: the dashboard. It has region, category and date-range filters; tiles for total revenue, orders and units sold; a monthly revenue bar chart and a category revenue bar chart, both with hover tooltips; and a table of the latest 50 matching orders. Changing a filter updates everything without reloading the page, and the filters are kept in the URL so a filtered view can be shared.
- **`GET /api/summary`**: returns exactly the JSON shape in the spec. Filters combine with AND, date ranges include both ends, and when nothing matches you get zeros and empty arrays.
- **Extra endpoints** I added: `/api/orders` (feeds the table), `/api/options` (fills the filter lists) and `/healthz` (a health check for deployment).
- **One choice of mine:** a malformed `start` or `end` date returns `400` with an error message. The spec doesn't say what to do in that case.

**How I checked it:**
- The tests compare the API's numbers against a separate simple calculation for no filters, all four filters combined, a single-day range, a filter that matches nothing, and a bad date.
- With curl, the unfiltered summary returned 2,400 orders, 15,179 units and $1,839,455.69 across all 12 months.
- I opened the page in headless Chrome with a region filter applied and the KPIs, both charts and the table all displayed correctly.

**To run it:**
```bash
npm start          # serves on $PORT, default 8080 → http://localhost:8080/
npm test           # runs the tests with Node's built-in test runner
```
final_messages.deploy:
The dashboard is live at **https://adb-kb60n-dataviz-cdqxy.ondigitalocean.app**, and every requirement in `TASK.md` works through that URL.

**What's running:**
- **App Platform app `adb-kb60n-dataviz`:** one web service, `adb-kb60n-dataviz-web`, on the Basic `apps-s-1vcpu-0.5gb` plan at $5/month. It runs the Docker image and gets HTTPS automatically on the `ondigitalocean.app` address. It's the cheapest option that can run a server; the free tier only hosts static files, which can't serve `/api/summary`.
- **Container registry `adb-kb60n-dataviz`:** the free starter tier, holding the image in a repository named `adb-kb60n-dataviz-web`.
- **Total:** about $5/month.

**What I tested on the public URL:**
- **`/api/summary`:** for six filter combinations it returned exactly the numbers I computed locally from the CSV. These were no filters, one filter, all filters combined, a single-day range, and queries that match nothing (zeros and empty arrays).
- **Bad date:** a malformed date returns 400.
- **The dashboard:** I opened `/` in headless Chrome with a category and start date in the URL. The filters, KPI tiles, both charts and the latest-50 orders table all showed the filtered results.

Nothing needed a person, so `human_steps` in `deployment.json` is empty. I didn't create any new credentials; the deploy used the token from your environment. To redeploy after changes, run `./deploy.sh`.

deployment_manifest.notes: Node.js server (no dependencies) holding data/sales.csv in memory, packaged as a Docker image in DOCR and run on App Platform. HTTPS uses App Platform's default ondigitalocean.app domain, and the health check is /healthz. Checked through the public URL: GET / renders the dashboard with filters, KPI tiles, both charts and the table of the latest 50 orders. GET /api/summary matched the local aggregation exactly for unfiltered, single-filter, combined-filter, inclusive single-day and no-match queries (no-match returns zeros and empty arrays). A malformed date returns 400. Redeploy with ./deploy.sh. App Platform's free tier only covers static sites, which can't serve /api/summary, so the $5 Basic service is the cheapest option that runs a server.
